title: Tortilla Española
subtitle: Spanish potato and egg omelette
excerpt: Tortilla española is the national dish of Spain: a thick round omelette of potato and egg, cooked slowly in olive oil and flipped. It is eaten warm, at room temperature, or cold, and is served in wedges at any meal. The potato must be confited in olive oil, not boiled or fried; this creates the characteristic soft, yielding texture.
sourceNotes: Tortilla española (not to be confused with the Mexican corn flatbread) appears in Spanish records from the early 19th century, though its origin is debated. It is eaten throughout Spain at any time of day: as tapas, in bocadillos (sandwiches), or as a main course. The version with onion (con cebolla) is considered superior to the version without.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tortilla is excellent at room temperature and improves after 30 minutes of resting. Can be made up to 4 hours ahead.

content.text: The flip is the difficult step: you need a plate or flat lid larger than the frying pan, press it firmly onto the pan with one hand, and invert quickly in one motion. A 22 to 24 cm non-stick pan is ideal. The potato confiting takes time. The potato slices should be completely soft before the egg is added.

items.prepNote: peeled, halved, very thinly sliced (2 to 3 mm)
for confiting; most is drained off after cooking

content.text: Pour the olive oil into the frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the potato slices and onion. They should be submerged or nearly so. Season generously with salt. Cook gently, stirring occasionally, for 20 to 25 minutes until the potato is completely soft but not coloured. The oil should bubble gently around the potato, not fry it at high heat.
Drain the potato and onion in a sieve set over a bowl, reserving the oil. Let the potato cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl. Season with salt. Add the warm potato and onion and fold together gently. Leave to rest for 2 minutes so the potato can absorb the egg.

Return 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil to the pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture. Flatten the top gently. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the edges are set and the base is golden.

Place a flat plate or lid firmly over the pan. Flip the tortilla onto the plate in one confident motion. Slide it back into the pan, raw-side down. Cook for 3 to 4 more minutes until set but with a slight wobble in the centre. Rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: Tortilla sticks to the pan when flipping
items.cause: Pan not non-stick enough, or not enough oil on the second side
items.fix: A non-stick pan is important here. After adding the oil for the second side, swirl it around before sliding the tortilla back in. A well-seasoned cast-iron pan also works.

items.symptom: Centre is raw after the stated time
items.cause: Tortilla was too thick, or heat was too low
items.fix: The tortilla should not be more than 3 to 4 cm thick. Increase the heat slightly. A 1-minute wobble in the centre is correct: carryover heat finishes it while resting.
